articles.title: Wi-Fi shows connected but pages will not load
articles.problem_description: The device reports it is connected to the wireless network but websites and apps do not load, or the status says no internet access.
steps: Turn Wi-Fi off and on again, or toggle airplane mode.
Forget the network and reconnect, entering credentials again.
Renew the IP lease (Windows: ipconfig /release then /renew; macOS: renew DHCP lease in network settings).
Test another device on the same network to see whether the problem is specific to this device.
Restart the device and retest in a different location.
articles.escalation: Escalate to network operations if several devices in the same area fail.
articles.source_note: Original sample article written for the XSupport AI project. Generic troubleshooting guidance; not copied from or representing any university policy, system or knowledge base.

articles.title: Wi-Fi keeps disconnecting in one location
articles.problem_description: Wireless drops repeatedly in a particular building, room or residence while working elsewhere.
steps: Record where and when the drops happen and which devices are affected.
Check whether the device roams between access points; forget and rejoin the network.
Update the wireless adapter driver or device operating system.
Test with a second device in the same spot.
If several people in the area report it, log the location and times for the network team.
articles.escalation: Repeated multi-user drops in one area indicate an access-point or coverage fault and need network operations.
articles.source_note: Original sample article written for the XSupport AI project. Generic troubleshooting guidance; not copied from or representing any university policy, system or knowledge base.

articles.title: VPN will not connect from off campus
articles.problem_description: The VPN client fails to connect, hangs on connecting, or disconnects soon after connecting.
steps: Confirm ordinary internet access works without the VPN.
Check the VPN client is the current version and restart it.
Confirm the account is not locked and multi-factor prompts are being approved.
Try a different network (for example a mobile hotspot) to rule out a home-network block.
Note the exact error text and time before escalating.
articles.escalation: Escalate with the error text if it persists on a second network.
articles.source_note: Original sample article written for the XSupport AI project. Generic troubleshooting guidance; not copied from or representing any university policy, system or knowledge base.

articles.title: Wall network port has no connection
articles.problem_description: A device plugged into a wall jack gets no link or no network access.
steps: Check both ends of the cable and try a different known-good cable.
Try another device on the same port, and the device on another port.
Check the link light on the network adapter.
Record the port label (printed on the wall plate) for the ticket.
Confirm the room is not affected by a wider outage.
articles.escalation: Dead port with a good cable and a working second device needs a network technician to check the switch port.
articles.source_note: Original sample article written for the XSupport AI project. Generic troubleshooting guidance; not copied from or representing any university policy, system or knowledge base.

articles.title: Websites are slow while the network seems connected
articles.problem_description: Pages load slowly or time out intermittently though the connection shows as active.
steps: Test several different sites to see whether one site or everything is slow.
Flush the DNS cache (Windows: ipconfig /flushdns).
Try another browser and disable extensions temporarily.
Compare with another device on the same network.
Note the time and location in case it matches a wider network issue.
articles.escalation: Slow performance across many users points to a network or DNS service problem.
articles.source_note: Original sample article written for the XSupport AI project. Generic troubleshooting guidance; not copied from or representing any university policy, system or knowledge base.

articles.title: Network down for a whole building or area
articles.problem_description: Several people in the same building or area report no network at the same time.
steps: Collect reports and note the building, floor and start time.
Check the service status page or announcements for known incidents.
Confirm at least two different devices in different rooms are affected.
Link new tickets to the same incident rather than troubleshooting each device.
Escalate promptly with the list of affected locations.
articles.escalation: Escalate immediately to network operations as a major incident.
articles.source_note: Original sample article written for the XSupport AI project. Generic troubleshooting guidance; not copied from or representing any university policy, system or knowledge base.

articles.title: Account locked after failed sign-ins
articles.problem_description: A user cannot sign in because the account has been locked after repeated failed attempts.
steps: Verify the user's identity using the approved verification procedure.
Check whether the lock is from failed attempts or a security hold.
If it is a standard lockout, unlock the account or wait for the lockout period to end.
Ask the user to update saved passwords on phones and other devices that may be retrying.
Record the unlock in the ticket.
articles.escalation: A lock caused by a security hold or suspicious activity goes to the security team.
articles.source_note: Original sample article written for the XSupport AI project. Generic troubleshooting guidance; not copied from or representing any university policy, system or knowledge base.

articles.title: Forgotten password reset
articles.problem_description: A user has forgotten their password and cannot sign in.
steps: Direct the user to the self-service password reset if it is available to them.
If not, verify identity with the approved procedure before any reset.
Issue a temporary password through a secure channel and require a change at next sign-in.
Remind the user to update saved credentials on other devices.
Document the reset without recording the password.
articles.escalation: Unverifiable identity: do not reset; escalate to a supervisor.
articles.source_note: Original sample article written for the XSupport AI project. Generic troubleshooting guidance; not copied from or representing any university policy, system or knowledge base.

articles.title: Multi-factor authentication on a new phone
articles.problem_description: A user changed phone or lost their authenticator and cannot complete multi-factor sign-in.
steps: Verify the user's identity using the approved procedure.
Remove or reset the old authentication method according to procedure.
Guide the user to register the authenticator app on the new phone.
Have the user test a sign-in before closing the ticket.
Suggest registering a backup method.
articles.escalation: Lost device with possible account exposure: involve the security team.
articles.source_note: Original sample article written for the XSupport AI project. Generic troubleshooting guidance; not copied from or representing any university policy, system or knowledge base.

articles.title: Cannot sign in to a student portal
articles.problem_description: A student cannot access the student portal although other services may work.
steps: Confirm the username format and that caps lock is off.
Try a private browser window to rule out cached sign-in data.
Check whether the account is active and not locked.
Confirm whether the portal itself has a known outage.
Reset the password if verified and appropriate.
articles.escalation: Account active but portal access still denied: escalate to the application owner.

articles.title: Microsoft 365 sign-in failure
articles.problem_description: A user cannot sign in to Microsoft 365 apps such as email, Teams or Office.
steps: Check the service health page for a known incident.
Confirm the account is active, unlocked and licensed.
Sign out of all Office apps, clear cached credentials and sign in again.
Try the web version in a private window.
If many users are affected, link to the incident.
articles.escalation: Multiple users failing at once is an incident: escalate to the collaboration platform team.

articles.title: Not receiving email or mailbox full
articles.problem_description: A user is not receiving messages or senders receive bounce messages.
steps: Check mailbox storage and ask the user to clear space if full.
Look in junk and quarantine folders.
Check mail rules and forwarding for unexpected entries.
Ask the sender for the exact bounce message.
Check message trace for the sender and time.
articles.escalation: Unexpected forwarding rules may indicate compromise: involve the security team.

articles.title: Shared calendar or shared mailbox not appearing
articles.problem_description: A shared calendar or shared mailbox does not show up or does not sync.
steps: Confirm the user has been granted access and when.
Allow time for permissions to propagate, then restart the mail client.
Remove and re-add the shared item.
Test in the web client to rule out client problems.
Re-apply the permission if it is missing.
articles.escalation: Permission changes need approval from the mailbox owner.

articles.title: Teams meeting audio or video problems
articles.problem_description: Microphone, speakers or camera do not work in Teams meetings.
steps: Check the correct devices are selected in Teams settings and run a test call.
Confirm the operating system has allowed Teams to use the microphone and camera.
Close other apps that may hold the device.
Update or restart Teams, then reboot if needed.
Try joining from the web client.
articles.escalation: Hardware fault on the device itself goes to hardware support.

articles.title: Printer offline, jammed or showing an error
articles.problem_description: A shared printer does not print, shows an error, or appears offline.
steps: Check the printer panel for paper jams, empty trays or toner messages.
Power cycle the printer and wait for it to be ready.
On the computer, remove the stuck job from the print queue and retry.
Confirm the computer is using the correct printer entry.
Try a different computer to see whether the issue is the printer or the PC.
articles.escalation: Hardware error codes that persist need printer maintenance.

articles.title: Installing or adding a printer
articles.problem_description: A user cannot add a network printer or the installation fails.
steps: Confirm the printer's network name or address.
Add the printer from system settings using the correct driver.
Check whether the user has permission to install printers.
Print a test page.
Record the printer name used.
articles.escalation: Driver deployment problems need desktop engineering.

articles.title: Laptop battery not charging or screen problems
articles.problem_description: A laptop does not charge, drains quickly, or has a faulty display.
steps: Try a known-good power adapter and outlet.
Remove external devices and check the charging port for debris.
Check power settings and battery health in the operating system.
Connect an external monitor to tell display faults from graphics faults.
Back up important data if hardware failure is likely.
articles.escalation: Confirmed battery or panel fault: arrange repair or a loaner device.

articles.title: Keyboard, mouse or monitor not responding
articles.problem_description: A peripheral does not respond or a monitor shows no signal.
steps: Check cables are firmly connected at both ends.
Try a different USB port or cable.
Test the peripheral on another computer.
For a monitor, confirm the correct input source is selected.
Replace the peripheral if it fails on a second computer.
articles.escalation: Replacement stock is requested through the normal equipment process.

articles.title: Lab workstation will not start
articles.problem_description: A shared lab computer does not boot, hangs on start, or is unresponsive.
steps: Check power cable and monitor connection.
Hold the power button to force off, wait, then start again.
Note any on-screen error or beep pattern.
Check whether other lab machines are affected.
Tag the machine as out of service if it cannot be fixed on the spot.
articles.escalation: Hardware faults or imaging failures go to desktop support.

articles.title: Classroom projector shows no image
articles.problem_description: The projector does not respond, shows no image, or does not display the connected laptop.
steps: Confirm the projector is powered and not in standby; use the room control panel.
Select the correct input source.
Check the cable from the laptop and try a different adapter.
Set the laptop to extend or duplicate the display.
Try the room's podium computer to separate laptop issues from projector issues.
articles.escalation: Lamp or hardware faults need AV technicians on site.

articles.title: No sound in a classroom
articles.problem_description: Speakers produce no sound during class presentations.
steps: Check the room volume and that the system is not muted.
Confirm the audio source and output are selected correctly on the computer.
Check microphone and speaker cables and power.
Test with a different source.
Report the room number and what was tested.
articles.escalation: Persistent room audio failure needs an AV technician.
articles.source_note: Original sample article written for the XSupport AI project. Generic troubleshooting guidance; not copied from or representing any university policy, system or knowledge base.

articles.title: Podium computer frozen or laptop will not connect to screen
articles.problem_description: The teaching station computer is frozen or cannot log in, or a laptop cannot be shown on the room screen.
steps: Restart the podium computer if it is frozen and safe to do so.
Confirm the user's account can sign in elsewhere.
For laptops, check the cable, adapter and display input selection.
Use the room's guide for the input switcher.
Report the room and the symptoms.
articles.escalation: On-site AV or desktop support if a restart does not help.

articles.title: Lecture recording did not upload
articles.problem_description: A lecture capture session finished but the recording is missing or stuck.
steps: Check the schedule matched the room and time.
Check whether the recording shows as processing; allow time.
Confirm the capture device in the room was powered and online.
Record the course, room and time of the missing session.
Ask the instructor to check the recording library.
articles.escalation: Missing recordings need the lecture-capture administrator.

articles.title: Application freezes or crashes
articles.problem_description: An application hangs or closes unexpectedly on Windows or macOS.
steps: Note the application, version and what the user was doing.
Restart the application and the computer.
Install pending updates for the application and operating system.
Test with a new user profile or after clearing application cache.
Check available disk space and memory.
articles.escalation: Reproducible crashes with an error log go to the software owner or vendor.

articles.title: Software says licence expired
articles.problem_description: An application reports an expired or missing licence.
steps: Confirm the user is signed in with the correct work account.
Sign out and in again to refresh the licence.
Check the user is assigned the licence in the licensing portal.
Update the application to the current version.
Request a licence if none is assigned.

articles.title: Operating system update will not install
articles.problem_description: A system update fails, loops or stalls.
steps: Check free storage and battery or power connection.
Restart and retry the update.
Check the update service or settings for an error code.
Disconnect nonessential peripherals.
Back up data before further repair attempts.
articles.escalation: Repeated failure with an error code may need a reinstall by desktop support.

articles.title: Website error in one browser
articles.problem_description: A web application or course site fails in one browser but may work in another.
steps: Try a private window and another browser.
Clear cache and cookies for the site.
Disable extensions such as ad blockers.
Update the browser.
Note the exact error message and URL.
articles.escalation: If it fails everywhere, report to the site owner.

articles.title: Suspicious or phishing email
articles.problem_description: A user received an email asking for a password or sign-in that looks suspicious, or clicked a link.
steps: Tell the user not to click links or open attachments.
Ask whether they entered credentials or opened an attachment.
If credentials were entered, treat as a possible compromise and follow that article.
Report the message to the security team using the approved route.
Delete the message after it has been reported.
articles.escalation: Any entered credentials or opened attachment: escalate to security immediately.

articles.title: Suspected account compromise
articles.problem_description: A user sees unknown sign-ins or believes their account was hacked.
steps: Verify identity and confirm what activity looks unusual.
Reset the password and sign out all sessions per procedure.
Check mailbox rules and forwarding.
Confirm multi-factor methods are the user's own.
Notify the security team.
articles.escalation: Always involve the security team for confirmed or likely compromise.

articles.title: Lost or stolen device with account access
articles.problem_description: A phone, laptop or tablet that can access work accounts is lost or stolen.
steps: Record what the device was and what it could access.
Sign out sessions and reset the password as per procedure.
Start remote lock or wipe if the device is managed.
Report the loss to the security team.
Advise the user about reporting to campus security if appropriate.
articles.escalation: Escalate to security at once.

articles.title: Suspected malware or antivirus alert
articles.problem_description: Pop-ups, unusual slowness or an antivirus alert suggest malware.
steps: Disconnect the device from the network if the risk is high.
Do not delete or ignore the alert; record its text.
Run a full antivirus scan using the managed tool.
Change passwords from a different clean device if credentials may be exposed.
Report to the security team.
articles.escalation: Escalate to security for confirmed detections.

articles.title: Documents shared with the wrong people
articles.problem_description: A file or folder was shared with unintended recipients.
steps: Identify what was shared and with whom.
Remove the sharing links or permissions.
Check access logs if available.
Assess the sensitivity of the content.
Report to the security or privacy contact if sensitive data was exposed.
articles.escalation: Exposure of sensitive data must be reported to security or privacy.
